purpose: Author-facing rules for CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1 only. Backend/internal rules are intentionally omitted.

rules.instruction: Use only values published in this CURRENT. Absence from CURRENT means unavailable; never infer a handle or identity.
For locationHandle, visible.handle, effectHandle, viaHandle and audio.handle use an exact CURRENT Simple V1 authoring handle. Never serialize a raw Catalog asset ID.

animationIntent is the only field that requests an exact compatible animation capability. performanceIntent is descriptive directing intent and does not independently request or grant an Animation clip. Raw Animation identities remain backend compatibility vocabulary and are not direct Simple V1 handles.

Within one beat, explicit actions[].animationIntent is the animation owner for that Actor and suppresses inferred/default animation from other actions for the same Actor. Movement, fire and camera motion may still run concurrently; Unity owns collision-free backend action IDs.
Every dialogue speaker/listener must be an authoringReady actorId from EMOTIONAL_DIALOGUE_CURRENT.json and match cast[].id exactly.
For dialogue cast, cast[].identityHandle must exactly equal that character's published identityHandle. Do not substitute Actor, UI, Atlas or portrait handles.

expressionIntent, when present, must exactly match a supported expression for that speaker. Omit expressionIntent to request the published defaultExpression. Never fall back to Neutral for an unsupported explicit expression.
Do not combine locked portrait dialogue with explicit world movement for the same participant in the same beat. Put world movement in a separate beat when needed.
A cast participant has one narrative identity and at most one optional presentationHandle. presentationHandle never creates or changes identity.
Before selecting a visual handle, inspect its published Atlas pixels. Direct visual handles expose atlasPage and atlasSlot so no FULL_VISUAL_INDEX lookup is required for normal authoring.

Do not author V3/V5 bookkeeping such as lifetime ownership, mechanical IDs, fixed Dialogue Stage mechanics, project font defaults, deterministic scale defaults or raw presentation modes. Those remain backend-owned unless represented by a Simple V1 field.
camera.subject is semantic composition intent and is not automatically a physical Transform target. DialoguePortrait participants do not become WorldActors merely to satisfy camera targeting.

Follow and Track require one resolvable WorldActor target. Author camera.subject when the beat contains multiple possible Actor targets; when omitted and exactly one cast Actor is referenced by the beat actions, Unity resolves that Actor deterministically. Never author backend targetEntityId.
Actor motionIntent=orbit uses current V5 fixed-center Orbit. The center/target actor must remain stationary for the Orbit interval. Moving-center Orbit is not supported.

Simple V1 action objects may use explicit startOffset/duration, but actions[] array order is never a sequencing language. Use legal explicit intervals for staggering or concurrency. Distinct semantic locomotion phases such as approach/pass/bank/exit should use adjacent beats unless one continuous precise path represents them unambiguously; one primary locomotion phase may coexist with compatible timed fire/impact/reveal events.
Use semantic speed values slow, medium, fast or burst. Do not author numeric runtime speed values.

V1 owns WHAT: author only legal CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1 semantic intent. V4 owns HOW: internal directing/execution recipes may implement an already-legal V1 request, but V4 recipe IDs must never grant Actor capability and must never be serialized into CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1.

Schema-exposed editingMoves are legal authoring fields and may be selected automatically by ChatGPT or forced explicitly. They reference existing consecutive beats and do not silently rewrite authored beat IDs/order/durations. Current repertoire: EyelineMatch [LOOKER -> LOOKED_AT_OBJECT -> REACTION_LOOKER]: A looker, the looked-at object, then the same looker confirming the relation.; TravelThenReveal [TRAVEL -> DESTINATION_REVEAL -> SPATIAL_CONFIRMATION]: Visible travel, reveal the destination, then confirm traveler and destination share the established space.; ConvergingAction [ACTION_LINE_A -> ACTION_LINE_B -> CONVERGENCE]: Two distinct lines of visible action resolve into one shared frame or encounter.; KuleshovAssociation [SUBJECT -> ASSOCIATED_IMAGE -> SUBJECT_RETURN]: The same subject surrounds an associated image so the audience infers a subjective or emotional relation.; ParallelCrossCut [LINE_A -> LINE_B -> RETURN_A]: Alternate two distinct lines of action and return to the first so the audience infers simultaneity or comparison.; MatchOnAction [ACTION_START -> ACTION_CONTINUATION -> ACTION_RESULT]: Carry one subject's visible action across a cut so motion continuity joins different framings.; RevealThenReaction [REVEAL -> REACTION -> SHARED_CONTEXT]: Reveal new information, cut to a visible reaction, then restore shared context between cause and reactor.

Recoverable system-owned presentation or staging omissions remain warnings when the backend can resolve a legal deterministic default. Do not invent assets or backend fields to silence them. Real identity, CURRENT, capability or unsupported-expression failures remain blockers.
Serialize only fields defined by CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1.schema.json. Do not invent noncanonical fields.
